STEP 1 — goal: fix the design space for one paper-simple, level-1-only idea, avoiding the four already-refuted arms (cross-graph dual-segment transfer, capacity units, per-code curvature field, stratified-curvature + hyperbolic Sinkhorn, branching radial coordinates, parent-curvature, anchor ladder, taper innovation, dual-ramp capacity, sign-curvature ladder, geodesic successor drift).
What I read: my workspace (only progress.jsonl, empty) — no geometry contract file is readable from this sandbox, so I use the curvature conventions restated verbatim in the round text: ball of curvature kappa=-c, c>0, radius R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||), Euclidean tangent coordinate norm is NOT the Riemannian norm.
Reasoning that led to the choice: the round prescribes a minimal mechanism (scale-normalised level-1 residual lifted by exp_0^c; baseline anchors lifted by the same map; level-1 distance d_c; behaviour demand q_k frozen from training transitions; level-1 assignment argmin_k(D_k - off_k); levels 2,3, losses, STE identical to baseline; behaviour-off => constant offset; geometry-off => c=0 => 2*||u-q||). That skeleton is not in the rejected list, so it is admissible. My distinct contribution inside it: (a) the behaviour term is made zero-mean and dimensionless (z_k = log(1+demand_k) - mean) so that behaviour-off collapses exactly to the baseline argmin, not merely to a constant; (b) popularity-adjusted demand (in-degree divided by sqrt of successor degree) so hubs do not swamp the margin; (c) the coupling weight is DERIVED, not swept: w = theta * mean_k d_c / rms_k(z_k) with theta=0.1 as documented default, i.e. the maximum margin is 10% of the typical level-1 geodesic coding distance, automatically rescaled by the curvature scale 2/sqrt(c); (d) the margin is measured in hyperbolic distance units, so the change is literally a displacement of level-1 geodesic Voronoi bisectors (behaviour-shifted half-spaces), which is geometric computation, not a suffix.
Scope check performed: BEHAVIOUR yes (directed training-split transitions -> level-1 demand); GEOMETRY yes (exp_0^c, Möbius addition, d_c, c>0, curvature acts on level-1 assignment); COUPLING yes (single argmin uses both terms, removing either changes which codeword is selected and therefore which anchor receives gradient); TESTABLE yes (level-1 usage histogram, prefix conditional log-likelihood, Stage3 test recall@10; three switches exist, none trained off); SPECIFICATION yes (equations, dims, gradient rules, safeguards, cost).
Open: write the full block and the matching JSON answer.

STEP 2 (final) — the complete answer, block format.

IDEA: GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-shifted hyperbolic Voronoi bisectors for the level-1 RQ-VAE semantic ID: a training-only transition-demand margin added to the Poincare distance, with a scale-derived weight.
MOTIVATION: the level-1 codeword decides the first SID token and hence the whole prefix; the baseline picks it by Euclidean nearest-anchor, so two items whose successors are interchangeable but whose embeddings sit on opposite sides of a bisector get different prefixes. Behavioural co-transition information is available at training time yet never enters the assignment, and the assignment lives in flat space although the SID tree it induces is hierarchical/curved.
NOVELTY: prior arms moved curvature per code (OCCURV-FIELD), per stratum (strataot-curv-rq, with Sinkhorn), radially per branch (brancurv-l1-rq), or as a parent/anchor ladder. Here the curvature is a single fixed c and the behaviour enters as a displacement of the level-1 geodesic Voronoi bisectors measured in hyperbolic distance units; the weight is derived from the measured distance scale, and the behaviour term is zero-mean so behaviour-off is exactly the baseline argmin. No Sinkhorn, no per-code curvature, no radial coordinate, no capacity units, no cross-graph transfer.
CHANGE: the level-1 residual is lifted into the Poincare ball and compared to lifted baseline anchors with d_c, and the level-1 argmin subtracts a frozen zero-mean log-demand margin whose scale equals 10% of the typical level-1 geodesic coding distance; levels 2-3, all losses and the STE are unchanged.
SPECIFICATION: dims: M = baseline latent dim (32), K1 = baseline level-1 codebook size (256), 3 levels as baseline, forward: b = encoder(x); level1 residual r = b; s = RMS of ||b|| over the frozen pre-pass; u = exp_0^c(r/s); q_k = exp_0^c(a_k) with a_k the baseline level-1 codebook (same parameter tensor, no extra params for the quantizer); D_k = d_c(u,q_k); z_k = frozen zero-mean log-demand of code k; w = theta * Dbar / rms_k(z_k), theta = 0.1 documented; k1 = argmin_k (D_k - w*z_k) with ties to the smallest index; reconstruction and gradients exactly as baseline with the selected a_{k1}; z, w, s are buffers (no grad); levels 2-3 identical to baseline (Euclidean, same residual recursion, commitment and codebook losses). gradient_rules: dL/da_{k1} and dL/db are the baseline straight-through expressions (the selection index is a constant in the graph); no gradient flows into z, w or s; dL/du = -(2 dL/dD_{k1}) * d(d_c)/du with the standard Mobius derivative autodiffed. training_integration: compute s and z and Dbar in one frozen pre-pass over training data (baseline level-1 assignments, training-split transitions), store as buffers, then run the unchanged two-stage protocol with the modified level-1 argmin only. conventions: copied verbatim from HYPERBOLIC_GEOMETRY_CONTRACT: ball curvature kappa=-c, c>0, R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||), the Euclidean tangent-coordinate norm is not the Riemannian norm.
COST: one-time pre-pass: ~24556 latents + |training transitions| ~ O(1e6) soft/hard level-1 lookups, seconds to <1 min, <0.5% of the run. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, batch ~1024, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): one exp map per sample (M ops) + K1=256 exp maps for anchors (cached per step) + 256 Mobius additions/artanh per sample ~ 1.7e8 flops per

step, i.e. +3-6% of the quantizer block and about +1-3% of step wall clock; zero extra parameters, no extra optimiser state, <50 MB extra memory. Total run overhead ~2% wall clock.
HYPOTHESIS: if transition demand carries prefix-predictive information that the Euclidean level-1 partition ignores, the demand-scaled geodesic margin reallocates a modest fraction (order 5-15%) of level-1 assignments toward transition-central codes and raises Stage3 test recall@10 above 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best so far 0.0638); it would be observed as (i) a level-1 usage-histogram shift positively correlated with z_k, (ii) a higher conditional log-likelihood of the next SID token given the level-1 prefix on held-out prefixes, (iii) the recall gain. If the histogram does not move, the margin is too small relative to the geodesic distance spread and the hypothesis is falsified in one run.
RISKS: fixity of c and of theta=0.1 (no sweep allowed) means the margin may be too weak to move any argmin or so strong that level-1 usage collapses onto hub codes; artanh saturation near the ball boundary can make d_c numerically stiff and dominate the margin; degree-normalised demand may be too smooth to differentiate codes; level-1 may already be saturated so no headroom exists; the improvement may be real in prefix predictability but too small to lift Stage3 recall above 0.065 given single-seed noise; a mismatch between the frozen pre-pass assignments and the moving encoder can make the margin stale late in training.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: directed training-set item-to-item transition mass projected onto level-1 codewords (behaviour "demand" of each level-1 code), popularity-adjusted by the successor degree.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: from the TRAINING split only: for every observed transition (i -> j) in the training sequences, take the level-1 assignment k1(j) produced by the frozen pre-pass encoder; accumulate demand_k = sum over (i->j) of (1/sqrt(deg(j))) * 1[k1(j)=k]; divide by a scalar so that mean_k demand_k = 1; then z_k = log(1+demand_k) - mean_m log(1+demand_m). One pass, frozen as a buffer, never back-propagated.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: the transition graph, the successor degrees, s and Dbar are computed exclusively from the training split; validation/test interactions are never read, never counted and never used to fit any buffer; z, s, w are frozen before Stage 2 training starts, so no optimisation step can see validation/test signal, and SID construction uses no test-time popularity or co-occurrence.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: fixed negative curvature kappa=-c, c>0 (c=1 by default, so R_c=1); operations exp_0^c, Mobius addition, and the Poincare distance d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||); all in the level-1 quantizer.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: inside the level-1 assignment step of the RQ-VAE quantizer, during Stage 2 training (and unchanged at inference) — the distance that decides the first SID token.
COUPLING PATH: one argmin: k1 = argmin_k [ d_c(u, exp_0^c(a_k)) - w*z_k ], where u = exp_0^c(r/s); the behaviour term z_k is added to the geodesic distance in the same scalar comparison, so removing behaviour collapses the comparison to baseline nearest-anchor and removing curvature replaces d_c by the flat distance and therefore changes the effective meaning and scale of the same margin (w is derived from Dbar, which itself changes) — the selection index, hence the STE gradient path, changes in both ablations.
COUPLING EQUATION: k1 = argmin_k [ (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqr

t(c)*|| (-exp_0^c(r/s)) (+) exp_0^c(a_k) ||) - w * ( log(1+demand_k) - mean_m log(1+demand_m) ) ], with w = 0.1 * mean_k d_c / rms_k(z_k).
OBSERVABLES: level-1 codeword usage histogram and its correlation with z_k; mean level-1 geodesic residual radius; fraction of samples whose level-1 index changes relative to the baseline-style nearest-anchor; prefix conditional log-likelihood of the next SID token given the level-1 prefix on held-out prefixes; Stage3 test recall@10 (judgement only).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: z_k := 0 for all k (equivalently demand_k := 1, off_k := 0), so the level-1 argmin is exactly the pure geodesic nearest-anchor; switch present in code (flag BEHAVIOUR_ON=False), not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c := 0 path: exp_0^c becomes identity, d_c becomes 2*||u-q_k|| (Euclidean), Dbar recomputed in the same flat units so w stays scale-consistent, everything else identical; switch present in code (flag GEOMETRY_ON=False), not trained in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: behaviour margin and curvature both active — the single run of this round.
SPEC EQUATIONS: s = sqrt(mean_{x in T} ||b(x)||^2); u = tanh(sqrt(c)*||r/s||) * (r/s) / (sqrt(c)*||r/s||) with u=0 when ||r/s||=0; q_k = exp_0^c(a_k); M(x,y) = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2) x + (1-c||x||^2) y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2); D_k = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(clip(sqrt(c)*||M(-u,q_k)||, 0, 1-1e-6)); demand_k = (1/Z)*sum_{(i->j) in T} deg(j)^(-1/2) * 1[k1(j)=k], Z s.t. mean_k demand_k=1; z_k = log(1+demand_k) - mean_m log(1+demand_m); w = theta*Dbar/rms(z), theta=0.1; k1 = argmin_k (D_k - w*z_k), argmin ties -> smallest k; levels 2-3: (r2 = r - sg(a_{k1}) ... baseline recursion unchanged); loss = baseline recon + commitment; STE: grad to a_{k1} and to r as baseline, zero grad to z,w,s.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: inputs: batch embeddings b (B x M), baseline level-1 codebook a (K1 x M), c, frozen buffers s (scalar), z (K1), w (scalar), and the baseline levels 2-3. Outputs: level-1 index k1 (B,), the quantized level-1 vector a_{k1} (B x M) feeding the unchanged residual recursion, plus (diagnostic only) the per-sample D and the margin. Dtype float32 (float64 only in the frozen pre-pass).
SAFEGUARDS: clamp the radial argument sqrt(c)||v|| <= 10 before tanh; clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-6; clamp ||a_k|| <= 0.999*R_c and ||u|| <= 0.999*R_c; handle u == q_k with D=0 and a floor of 1e-9 under the square root and arctanh; z is zero-mean and RMS-normalised so w is finite (guard rms(z) < 1e-8 -> w=0); deterministic tie-break to the smallest index for reproducibility; no log of a non-positive demand (demand >= deg-normalised positive mass, and log1p used); frozen buffers stored outside the optimiser and asserted to have requires_grad=False; assert that the geometry-off path reproduces 2*||u-q|| exactly and that the behaviour-off path reproduces the baseline nearest-anchor indices on a fixed batch before training.
END IDEA

Caveat noted for review: the geometry contract file was not readable in this sandbox; all conventions were taken from the round text's verbatim restatement, which quotes that contract, so the signature is contract-faithful. Open: none.
